Metal Roofing in Dallas-Fort Worth

Thinking about a metal roof for a house, a barn or a shop? Call the free line and you are put through to an independent DFW roofing company that installs metal, so you can compare panels and prices with the facts below in hand.

  2. Services

Why metal keeps coming up in DFW roof conversations

After a hail season, a lot of North Texas homeowners start asking whether the next roof should be something other than asphalt shingles. Metal roofing in Dallas is one of the most common answers, along with the questions that come with it: which panel, which color, what it does in hail, whether the HOA will allow it and what it costs.

This page covers those questions with sourced facts so you can hold a useful conversation with a metal roofer. It does not sell metal, and neither does the line. DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone number whose automated assistant asks what you are planning and where, then transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that installs metal in your area. That company measures, recommends a panel and gives you a price in writing.

Metal is not automatically right for every house. A good roofer should be willing to tell you when a quality impact-rated shingle makes more sense for your budget or your neighborhood rules.

Standing seam, exposed fastener and other metal profiles

The biggest difference between metal roofs is how the panels are held down. That choice affects the look, the price, the upkeep and where the roof is allowed.

ProfileHow it attachesWhere you see itAsk about
Standing seamClips or fastening flanges hidden under raised seams that lock or snap together, so no screws go through the face of the panel.Houses, especially modern farmhouse and custom homes; some commercial roofs.Panel width and seam height, clip type (fixed or floating), the gauge, and how valleys and walls are flashed.
Exposed fastener (R-panel, PBR and similar ribbed panels)Screws with sealing washers driven through the flat of the panel into the framing or deck.Barns, shops, carports and pre-engineered metal buildings; some homes.Screw type and spacing, how often the washers should be checked, and whether the panel is approved for a house in your city.
Metal shingles and stone-coated steelSmaller interlocking pieces that mimic shingles, tile or shakes.Neighborhoods where an HOA prefers a traditional look.The impact rating, the look up close, and how the profile handles low-pitch areas.

Gauge is the panel's thickness: the lower the number, the thicker the steel. Some cities set a floor. Garland's re-roofing rules, for example, call for metal roofing of 26 gauge or heavier installed to the manufacturer's specifications, and a change of roofing material there needs a permit. Ask the bidder to name the gauge, the coating (galvanized or aluminum-zinc) and the paint system in writing.

Hail ratings and Texas insurance credits

What Class 4 means

UL 2218 tests a roofing product by dropping steel balls on it; to reach Class 4, the top rating, a sample has to survive a 2-inch steel ball dropped twice on the same spot without cracking through. The rating is about penetration, not looks. A Class 4 metal panel can still dent in a big storm, and dents show more on flat, glossy panels than on ribbed or textured ones.

The insurance side

The Texas Department of Insurance says insurers give credits for roofing rated under UL 2218, with Class 4 earning the largest, but each insurer sets its own amount and paperwork. Ask your insurer which tests it accepts and what proof it wants (the product label, TDI form PC068 filled out by the roofer, or both), how large the credit is, and whether your policy treats dents that do not leak as covered damage.

The insurer-funded research group IBHS has rated impact-resistant shingles with lab-made hailstones since 2019, which is a useful comparison if you are choosing between a metal roof and an impact-rated shingle. Ask any bidder for the product's test reports, not just a brochure.

Metal roof color ideas for North Texas houses

Color choice is partly taste and partly physics. Lighter colors, and darker pigments engineered as cool colors, bounce back more sunlight than ordinary dark paint, which can keep an attic cooler through a DFW summer. The way to compare is the product's tested solar reflectance and thermal emittance. The Cool Roof Rating Council publishes those values for rated products, and since ENERGY STAR stopped labeling roof products on June 1, 2022, the CRRC directory is the place to look rather than an ENERGY STAR sticker.

  • Charcoal, black and dark bronze suit modern farmhouse and contemporary homes; ask whether a cool-pigment version is offered.
  • Galvalume and light gray fit barns, shops and ranch homes and tend to be among the more reflective finishes.
  • Barn red, forest green and other classic colors appear on rural buildings across North Texas; check fade and chalk warranty terms for each color.
  • Brown and tan tones often blend best with brick and stone in suburban HOAs.

Before falling for a color, check the rules that apply. Fort Worth's design guidelines for the Fairmount historic district say metal roofs need a certificate of appropriateness, allow standing seam on secondary roof slopes and list R-panel and rib panel profiles as prohibited. Many HOAs keep an approved color list.

What a metal roof costs in Dallas-Fort Worth

Two published sources give very different numbers, and both are worth knowing. Angi's Dallas cost page reports an average metal roofing project of about $12,474, with a range from $4,118 to $20,829. The Journal of Light Construction's Cost vs. Value report for 2025 prices its model job, about 3,000 square feet of standing seam metal roofing on a hip roof, at $46,790 in Dallas, $44,505 for the West South Central region and $51,865 nationally, and estimates that about 49 percent of the Dallas cost is recouped at resale. The difference comes from what each one measures: Angi averages jobs of all sizes, including small buildings and partial roofs, while the Cost vs. Value job is a complete standing seam roof on a fairly large house.

Panel profile, gauge, roof complexity (valleys, dormers, chimneys), tear-off and decking repairs, underlayment, trim and the paint system all move the number. None of these figures is a price from the line or from any roofer, and real quotes vary. Get every bid itemized so you can compare one panel system with another.

Say "metal roof" when the assistant asks what you need, and mention whether it is for a house, a barn or shop, or a business, and your town. The roofing company you are connected with can bring panel samples and color charts to the estimate.

Questions to ask a metal roofer before you sign

  1. Which panel, gauge and coating? Brand, profile, thickness, metallic coating and paint system, in writing.
  2. What is the impact rating? Ask for the UL 2218 class and the label or test report your insurer may ask to see.
  3. What goes under the panels? Tear-off or not, decking repairs, the underlayment and how ventilation will work.
  4. How are the details handled? Valleys, walls, chimneys, pipe penetrations and ridge closures are where metal roofs leak.
  5. Which warranties apply? The panel maker's paint and finish warranty, any weathertightness warranty, and the installer's own workmanship terms.
  6. Does the city or HOA need to approve it? Who pulls the permit, and is written HOA approval in hand before work starts?

If you own acreage in Parker, Hood, Johnson or Ellis County and want a house, barn and shop roofed at the same time, say so on the call; some roofers handle residential panels and agricultural buildings, and some do only one.

How a metal roofing call works

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. Metal roof questions DFW homeowners ask

What are the benefits of a tin roof?

What people call a tin roof today is almost always coated steel or aluminum. Its draws are long service life, few seams for water to find, panels that shed rain quickly, and the option of reflective colors that take some heat off the attic. Some panels carry a UL 2218 Class 4 impact rating, which can earn an insurance credit in Texas. Downsides: a higher upfront price than shingles, and hail can dent panels even when they do not leak.

What is the best color for a metal roof in Texas?

There is no single best color. Lighter and specially formulated cool colors reflect more sunlight, which helps in a North Texas summer, and the Cool Roof Rating Council publishes tested reflectance for specific products and colors. The other limits are practical: your HOA's approved palette, any historic district rules, and how the color looks with your brick or stone. Ask the roofer for the rated values of the exact color you like.

How much does a metal roof cost in Texas?

Published figures vary widely. Angi's Dallas page lists an average metal roofing job of about $12,474, with a range of $4,118 to $20,829, while the Journal of Light Construction's 2025 Cost vs. Value report puts its standing seam metal re-roof model job at $46,790 in Dallas and $44,505 across the West South Central region. The gap reflects different job sizes and panel types. Real quotes vary; get each bid itemized. The DFW roof cost guide explains what drives price.

Is a metal roof louder in a hailstorm or rain?

It depends on how it is built. A metal roof over solid decking, underlayment and an insulated attic is a very different thing from bare panels over open purlins on a barn. If noise matters to you, ask the roofer what will sit under the panels and whether you can visit a finished house with the same assembly before you decide.

Can my HOA stop me from putting on a metal roof?

Possibly. Under Section 202.011 of the Texas Property Code, an HOA generally cannot forbid certain impact-resistant, energy-efficient or solar shingles that resemble the approved ones, but the statute is written about shingles. For metal panels, read your deed restrictions and get written approval from the architectural committee before you sign a contract. The roofer cannot get that approval for you.

Weighing a metal roof? Talk it through with a local roofer

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
